subject: Weekly MAP close ops bulletin & go-live runbook alignment
messages:
From: Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@cardio.ai>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: acme-ops+map@acmecorp.com
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0000
Subject: MAP weekly checkpoint — target launch 2027-05-14?

Hi Grace / team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our execs want a single weekly checkpoint thread from here through cutover so we can track owners and outstanding blockers. Target go-live date remains 2027-05-14 (subject to final sign-off). A few items we need from Redwood this week: 

- Finalized cutover runbook (including revert points and expected downtime) — needed by end of week.
- Confirmation on model variant we’ll serve for production and the fallback model.
- Updated acceptance tests and the eval that will gate canary traffic.

Can we stand up a 30-min MAP sync next Tue or Wed? Jordan / Acme MAP team are available Wed 2027-04-28 afternoon ET.

Appreciate it,
Jordan

Jordan Patel
Product Lead, Integrations — Cardio.AI
jordan.patel@cardio.ai
+1 (415) 555-0199

[Attachment: acceptance_criteria_cardio_v1.xlsx]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@cardio.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai, acme-ops+map@acmecorp.com
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:07:00 -0000
Subject: Re: MAP weekly checkpoint — target launch 2027-05-14?

Jordan — thanks, that works.

We’ll run a standing 30-minute MAP checkpoint every Wednesday 16:00 ET (starting 2027-04-28) until cutover. Calendar invite sent to the group.

Quick status and owners (high level):

- Cutover runbook: draft attached (cutover-checklist.xlsx). Owner: Ben Carter — deliver v2 by 2027-04-28 EOD.
- Production model variant: Ben will confirm which quantized variant we’ll serve and the paired fallback model by 2027-04-29.
- Eval gating: David Kim owns the canary acceptance tests and will publish the eval suite and expected pass criteria by 2027-04-29.
- Procurement / SLA: Laura Bennett will circulate the final SLA and the DocuSign envelope.

Meeting agenda for Wednesday (30 mins):
1) Roll call + go/no-go checklist status (5m)
2) Runbook walkthrough + rollback points (10m)
3) Canary gating criteria + dashboards (10m)
4) Open blockers & next actions (5m)

Ask: Ben — please highlight any manual steps that require Acme ops on Wed.
David — include the smoke-test dashboard link in your update.
Laura — if procurement needs anything else pre-signature let us know.

Thanks — Grace

Grace O'Connor
Director, Partnerships & Launch — Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai | +1 (212) 555-0133
Redwood Inference

Cc: jordan.patel@cardio.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, acme-ops+map@acmecorp.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 21:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: MAP weekly checkpoint — target launch 2027-05-14?

Grace / Jordan —

Attaching the runbook and fallback procedures (go-live-runbook-v2.pdf; fallback-procedures.txt). Summary below: 

- Runbook highlights (new in v2):
  * Pre-cutover: KV cache warm-up step + verification (2k sample prompts). Owner: Ben Carter.
  * Cutover window: 03:00–03:20 UTC on 2027-05-14. Expected steakholder-visible latency bump for first 500 tokens while caches repopulate.
  * Revert point: Canary traffic toggle and instant rollback to fallback model (20s estimated).

- Model variant decision: we will serve quantized-8b-v1 (throughput optimized). Fallback: full-16b-compat. Confirmation saved in internal config; Ben to post commit hash by 2027-04-29.

- Manual steps requiring Acme: update DNS CNAME to point to new edge endpoint (planned automation, manual failback documented). Request: Acme ops to standby during cutover window for <30 minutes.

Open items / risks:
- Performance variance under peak prompts (we have a small repro test but need Acme production-like prompt mix). Action: David to run extended canary with 1M tokens by 2027-05-06.
- DocuSign SLA outstanding (Laura).

Attachments: go-live-runbook-v2.pdf (runbook), fallback-procedures.txt (short checklist).

Ben

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (617) 555-0147

Team — thanks for the updates and the runbook. Quick procurement / executive notes: 

- I’ve uploaded the final SLA to DocuSign (link below). Please review and confirm we have the operational metrics called out (SLOs, incident response, data retention).
- Executive pre-approval is conditional on: (1) successful canary eval by 2027-05-06; (2) Ben’s commit hash and rollback verification; (3) Acme confirms DNS standby.

If the three conditions above are green by 2027-05-07 EOD, I will issue formal go for the 2027-05-14 cutover and send the DocuSign request to Cardio.AI execs.

Open owners and deadlines (final):
- Ben Carter: runbook v2 uploaded; post commit hash + perf baseline by 2027-04-29 (STATUS: in progress).
- David Kim: publish canary eval plan + dashboard link by 2027-04-29; run extended canary by 2027-05-06 (STATUS: in flight).
- Jordan / Acme ops: confirm DNS standby & validate prompt mix sample by 2027-05-06.
- Laura Bennett: finalize DocuSign (in progress) — envelope: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/AB1234567890

Attachments: docusign-acme-sla.pdf. HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deals/ACME-234

Assuming we hit those gates, we’ll finalize the MAP on 2027-05-07 and ship canary the week of 2027-05-10.

Laura Bennett
